To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the P protein is a bifunctional protein with two distinct domains, one required for RNA synthesis and the other for nascent chain assembly, and that the latter domain is required to prevent NP from illegitimately assembling independently of the nascent chain.
the P protein of Sendai paramyxoxvirus contains two RNA synthesis domains and that the N-terminal domain of P acts as a chapeone for the NP during the nascent assembly step of genome synthesis.

a chaperone function is required for the nasent chain assembly step of Sendai virus genome replication, that this function is mediated by amino acids 33 through 41 of P, and that this chaperone domain is distinct from the two other domains involved in RNA replication which have been previously identified within the N-terminal region of P.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assembly of a nasent viral genome and the role of P in the process.
the identification and characterization of the functional domains of the P protein of Sendai virus which is responsible for the assembly of nascent viral genomes.
the molecular basis for the assembly of the Sendai viral genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P is required to form an assembly competent complex with the NP of the nascent chain, which is then delivered to the nascente chain to form an assembly complex with P and the nascent chain itself.
the P protein has two distinct domains involved in genome replication, one required for RNA synthesis and one required for nascent chain assembly.

the N-terminal region of P is a multifunctional domain, with two domains being involved in RNA synthesis and the third being a chaperone function required for the nasient chain assembly step of the genome replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
P has three distinct domains, one required for RNA synthesis, one for the nascent assembly step of genome synthesis, and one for the chaperone function.

the Sendai virus genome is replicated by a two-step process, the first step being the assembly of a stable NP-P complex which is delivered to a nascent genome, and the second step being the synthesis of the nascent viral genome.
P has two domains which are required for genome replication, one required for RNA synthesis and one required to prevent the illegitimate assembly of NP.
The main takeaway from our work is that

P has two separate and distinct functions in the assembly of the nascent chain of viral RNA during genome replication: one is required for mRNA synthesis and the other is required for the nascept chain assembly step.
the Sendai virus NP protein has two distinct chaperone functions.

P can be divided into at least three functional domains, one for each step of genome replication: the chaperone domain, which interacts with the nascent chain; a domain for RNA synthesis; and a domain for nucleocapsid assembly.
